papers.title: Chance-Constrained Inspection Viewpoint Sequencing for On-Orbit Servicing via Safe Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Autonomous inspection of a target spacecraft is typically the initial step in on-orbit servicing. Planning close-proximity observation viewpoints involves a complex combinatorial problem constrained by coverage, fuel, and safety considerations. This paper models the viewpoint selection as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP) and applies Proximal Policy Optimization with Lagrangian relaxation to solve it. The system combines a high-level planner, which sequences camera viewpoints on an observation sphere around the target, with a low-level model that assesses each transfer using the Clohessy--Wiltshire (CW) equations for relative motion. The deterministic constraints on single-impulse reachability and $\Delta v$ cap are enforced directly on the action set. Safety margins are affected by navigation and manoeuvre errors, making the actual clearance stochastic. To address this, a chance constraint on the realised trajectory is implemented, with a Lagrangian multiplier governed by PID control to adapt the penalty during training. The approach is tested on a Galileo-class navigation satellite in medium Earth orbit, modelled as a point cloud where visibility from each viewpoint considers field-of-view and line-of-sight occlusion. Across various risk budgets, the trained policy maintains the keep-out violation rate within the specified limit, achieving coverage close to its maximum and staying within the mission $\Delta v$ budget. Compared to the usual practice of applying a fixed margin to the keep-out radius and planning deterministically, the chance-constrained policy attains less than half the violation rate at comparable coverage. This makes the collision risk an explicit design parameter, eliminating the need for re-tuning per case. The learned policy selects a viewpoint without the repeated Monte Carlo risk estimates required by a greedy, chance-constrained planner at every decision point.
papers.title_ja: 安全強化学習を用いた軌道上サービスにおける確率制約付き点検視点シーケンス設計

papers.title: Risk-Sensitive Mission Planning for Multi-Target On-Orbit Inspection via Distributional Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Multi-target on-orbit servicing missions require planning tools that can adapt to evolving operational conditions while accounting for the outcome variability inherent to safety-critical spaceflight. This paper presents an adaptive planning approach for multi-target servicing campaigns in low Earth orbit and applies it to inspection missions flown by a low-thrust servicer. The approach is based on Distributional Reinforcement Learning, which learns the full distribution of mission returns and thereby supports explicit risk-sensitive decision-making at each planning step. Specifically, a Quantile-Regression Deep Q-Network (QR-DQN) agent selects which target to inspect next by jointly considering the expectation and the variance of the predicted return through a mean-variance criterion. The mission environment models circular orbits with a spread in inclination and uses Edelbaum's combined-manoeuvre low-thrust transfer estimates. The observation comprises the orbital elements, the visit history, the observed risk state of each target and the remaining mission-time budget. The risk state of each target changes stochastically during the campaign, making the outcome of an inspection uncertain and creating operationally meaningful distinctions between risk-neutral and risk-averse planning strategies. Because the mission-time budget generally admits only a subset of the candidate targets, the planner must also select which targets to inspect. Numerical experiments on scenarios with five target satellites show that one risk-aversion weight moves the policy across a range of mean return and return variance, over an unchanged environment and reward. Risk-averse agents reduce the variance of the episodic return by approximately one half relative to risk-neutral agents and lower the probability of a mission loss, at a cost in mean return. To validate the learned policies, the efficient frontier, which gives the highest mean return attainable at each level of return variance, is computed exactly by enumerating the admissible visit orders. At equal variance, the learned policies lie close to this frontier in mean return, and the risk-averse policies have a lower probability of a mission loss than the frontier policies.

papers.title: Integrating Low-Thrust Transfer Dynamics into POMDP Planning for On-Orbit Servicing
papers.summary: Recent developments in both high-thrust (HT) and low-thrust (LT) propulsion technologies broaden design options for on-orbit servicing (OOS) missions. However, incorporating LT transfers into OOS mission planning requires accounting for the trade-off between prescribed transfer duration and propellant consumption. Multi-servicing, multi-transfer OOS mission planning is inherently sequential and requires adaptive planning tools that account for propulsion-dependent transfer durations and mass-dependent propellant consumption. Thus, transfer dynamics must be integrated into mission planning and scheduling to increase flexibility and adaptability. In addition, the planning is often done with imperfect information about the system's state and stochastic service demands. This paper focuses on modeling orbital transfers, particularly LT transfers, within a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) framework for OOS mission planning. To enable offline policy computation, the transfer model must provide explicit state transitions and rewards for all admissible actions. The state space is therefore augmented with the servicing vehicle's remaining propellant to enable consistent mass updates. HT transfers are modeled using a precomputed transfer matrix that maps each transfer to the time of flight and propellant consumed. LT transfers are represented using an analytical GEO phasing model with prescribed transfer-duration alternatives. For each alternative, the model calculates propellant consumption and maneuver feasibility as functions of the required phase change and the current servicing-vehicle mass. The proposed modeling approach is evaluated on simplified OOS planning scenarios using circular phasing with HT and LT propulsion. The resulting POMDPs are solved using the Successive Approximations of the Reachable Space under Optimal Policies (SARSOP) algorithm, and the policies obtained under HT and LT are compared. This comparison provides a quantitative assessment of the feasibility and operational impact of LT options, particularly regarding the potential role of advanced electric propulsion in future servicing architectures.

papers.title: Kernel-based Interpolatory Methods for Context Compression of Attention Mechanisms
papers.summary: The bottleneck of attention mechanisms, which are the fundamental building block of modern language models, is their quadratic complexity in terms of context size. There has thus been an increasing interest in the compression of the context, also called KV-cache compression. In this article, we consider the problem of compressing the context of attention mechanisms by first formulating it in the Hilbert space associated with its kernel. In this formalism, attention can be represented as the ratio of two linear maps whose interpolant is also the ratio of interpolants, this allows us to consider the interpolation of the linear maps directly. We thus introduce two novel KV-cache compression methods which we call GAIM and Q-DAIM, based on the Generalized Empirical Interpolation Method (GEIM) and the Q-Discrete Empirical Interpolation Method (Q-DEIM), respectively. As the cost of these methods is quadratic in terms of context length, we propose surrogate models based on the Taylor series, the Performer and the Random Fourier Features method which allow the compression to be done in linear time. Finally, we extend this result to the streaming attention setting, providing new methods which allow one to penalize the selection of interpolation nodes based on the previously interpolated context and to update the previous interpolation based on new information. We then provide numerical results on the convergence of the residuals and the output error in future queries and preliminary results on the LongBench-E benchmark showing performance comparable to the state-of-the-art methods. These experiments suggest that the range revealed by our Q-DAIM method could help identify where information is concentrated in the KV cache, thus enabling an efficient compression.

papers.title: PDE-Residual-Informed Kriging
papers.summary: Physics-informed Gaussian process (GP) methods provide a probabilistic framework for PDE solving. Existing approaches incorporate PDE information in different ways: pointwise conditioning uses the governing equation only at finitely many selected locations, globally constrained GPs restrict the admissible functions to satisfy the PDE exactly, and residual-penalized methods control the PDE mismatch over the whole domain through an additional penalty weight. What is still missing is a GP formulation that directly incorporates global PDE-residual information of the entire domain into its covariance structure, while retaining model flexibility and standard GP conditioning without a separate residual-weight parameter. To solve this issue, this study proposes PDE-residual-informed Kriging (PRIK) based on a PDE-residual kernel. The PDE-residual kernel is constructed by equipping a kernel-section space with an inner product defined by the $L^{2}$ inner product of PDE residuals. This construction makes PRIK yield the posterior mean with minimum integrated squared PDE residual. It also provides direct statistical interpretations: the variance-scale estimate equals the normalized PDE-residual energy (i.e., the integrated squared PDE residual of the posterior mean divided by the number of labeled observations), and the profile likelihood balances this residual energy against model complexity. Under the stated regularity and stability conditions, we establish $H^{2}$-quasi-optimality and convergence rates for the posterior mean, together with a nonasymptotic bound for its PDE-residual norm. We further show that the normalized posterior kernel converges to a variational Green-type kernel and derive a uniform nonasymptotic contraction bound for the posterior variance. Numerical studies provide empirical evidence consistent with the theory and demonstrate the PDE-solving capability of PRIK.
papers.title_ja: PDE残差情報に基づくクリギング
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、偏微分方程式（PDE）の解法として、PDE残差情報を共分散構造に直接組み込むガウス過程（GP）手法「PDE残差情報クリギング（PRIK）」を提案する。従来の手法では残差ペナルティの重み付けが必要であったが、PRIKはPDE残差のL2内積を用いたカーネルを定義することで、このパラメータを不要にしつつ、後验平均が最小の積分二乗PDE残差を持つことを保証する。理論的には、後验平均のH^2準最適性や収束速度、非漸近的上界を導出し、数値実験によりその有効性を示している。

papers.title: When Does Jacobian Fine-Tuning Stabilize Neural PDE Emulators?
papers.summary: Neural emulators of chaotic PDEs are trained on one-step prediction but deployed autoregressively, where their errors compound. Jacobian-based regularisers aim to curb this growth, but in a chaotic system part of the growth is physical and cannot be trained away. We separate the two sources of this error with a first-order decomposition. We compare the emulator's error with a counterfactual that propagates the same one-step mistakes through the solver's Jacobian, giving an amplification ratio: the factor by which the model's own dynamics amplify its errors. We study 21 configurations across four PDEs, five architectures and two model sizes (8-10k and 33k parameters), with errors measured at one Lyapunov time. Jacobian fine-tuning reduced the error by more than 10% for 1 of 34 seeds whose amplification ratio was at most 1.25, and for all 20 seeds whose ratio was at least four; for the latter, the error fell by a factor of 8 (small models) and 55 (33k models) in geometric mean over seeds. The gain approximately equals the one-step accuracy cost of fine-tuning divided by the amplification ratio. Matching the solver's Jacobian along the model's own error direction (EDJM) outperformed random directions at the same cost on 28 of 35 seeds; input-noise injection performed comparably to EDJM.
papers.title_ja: ヤコビアン微調整はニューラルPDEエミュレータを安定化させるのか？

papers.title: Physics-Informed Latent Neural ODEs for Reduced-Order Modeling of Hydrogen, Ammonia, and Methane Combustion Kinetics
papers.summary: Detailed chemical kinetic mechanisms are computationally expensive in reacting-flow simulations because of their high dimensionality and numerical stiffness. We develop an end-to-end physics-informed autoencoder neural ordinary differential equation (PI-AE-NODE) framework in which an encoder compresses the thermochemical state into a low-dimensional latent space, a Neural ODE advances it continuously in time, and a decoder reconstructs the temperature and all species mass fractions. Elemental conservation, mass conservation, and enthalpy consistency are embedded in the training objective. The framework is applied to H$_2$/air, NH$_3$/air, and CH$_4$/air autoignition using detailed mechanisms of increasing size and complexity, which are represented accurately with only a few latent variables. Compared with an otherwise identical data-driven model, the physical constraints improve ignition delay prediction and conservation behaviour. The models reproduce major and intermediate species evolution at both training and unseen conditions, and their latent dynamics permit efficient explicit integration, with the computational advantage over the detailed mechanisms increasing with mechanism size.
papers.title_ja: 水素・アンモニア・メタン燃焼反応速度論の縮約モデリングのための物理情報潜在ニューラルODE

papers.title: Li$^{2}$SAO: Lifting Light Singl-Rollout Asynchronous RL Optimization via Group-Relative Actor-Critic Bootstrapping
papers.summary: Asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) is becoming a mainstream paradigm for post-training large language models (LLMs), as it improves training efficiency by updating the model as rollouts arrive. Recent work argues that group-wise sampling in GRPO does not naturally fit asynchronous RL training because rollout lengths follow a long-tailed distribution, and proposes Single-rollout Asynchronous Optimization (SAO) to improve stability and off-policy behavior, especially on agentic tasks. However, SAO relies on a closed-source value model obtained from scaling value pretraining. In this paper, we analyze GRPO and LiSAO, our lightweight reproduction of SAO without the pretrained value model, on single-turn reasoning and multi-turn agentic tasks. We find that GRPO outperforms LiSAO on reasoning tasks, while the reverse holds on agentic tasks. Since the value model of LiSAO is not yet well trained , LiSAO lags behind GRPO substantially in early training steps. To address this issue, we propose Li$^{2}$SAO, which Lifts Light Single-rollout Asynchronous Optimization with group-relative actor-critic bootstrapping: while the critic is cold, a group-relative advantage trains the actor and a group-centered return trains the critic, after which training switches to single-rollout GAE. Experiments show that Li$^{2}$SAO catches up with or surpasses GRPO in early training and further raises the later performance ceiling. Code is available at https://github.com/jd-cc-coder/Li2SAO.

papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）の非同期強化学習において、既存手法SAOが依存する事前学習済みバリューモデルの欠如問題を解決する。提案手法Li$^{2}$SAOは、クリティックモデルが未熟な初期段階でグループ相対アドバンテージを用いてアクターを訓練し、その後シングルロールアウトGAEへ切り替えるブートストラッピング戦略を採用する。これにより、推論タスクではGRPOを上回り、エージェントタスクではSAOの性能を早期に達成しつつ、最終的な性能上限も高めることを実験で示した。

papers.title: On the Origin and Evolution of Training-Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: On-policy reinforcement learning for large language models assumes that training responses are sampled from the current policy. In practice, an inference engine samples the responses and a separate trainer computes the gradients, and the \textbf{training-inference mismatch} between the two makes the training data off-policy. The mismatch has two sources, the numerics of the engine and the stale weights of asynchronous sampling, and a correction that stabilizes training under one source can fail under the other. \textit{We ask which property of a mismatch source decides the correction it needs.} Evaluating the trainer at the sampler's weights splits each sampled-token error exactly into a \textit{numerical discrepancy} of the engine and a \textit{policy lag} of the trainer, and we follow both through training. The numerical discrepancy stays approximately constant, so it biases the updates by a nearly fixed amount, and centering the score at each prefix removes its leading bias. The policy lag is produced by the trainer's own updates: the bias it leaves enters the next update, which enlarges the next lag and closes a feedback loop. Importance weighting cuts this loop only while the lag ratio stays concentrated, and on Qwen3-1.7B it fails at the step where the effective sample size of the ratio falls below one half. From this account we derive the \textbf{discrepancy-lag correction} (DLC), which centers the numerical discrepancy, clips the lag ratio against the sampler's weights and resynchronizes the sampler when this effective sample size falls below one half. Under a stale sampler, DLC keeps the KL divergence from on-policy training within twice the KL between two independent on-policy trainings on Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B, and its resynchronization prevents collapses that the per-token corrections leave and that a KL measured on the sampler's prefixes does not detect.
papers.title_ja: LLM強化学習における学習・推論ミスマッチの起源と進化について
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデルのオンポリシー強化学習において、推論エンジンと学習器の不一致（ミスマッチ）がオフポリシー化を引き起こす問題を分析する。数値的差異とポリシーラグという2つの要因を分離し、それぞれに対する補正手法の限界を特定した。特に、ポリシーラグがフィードバックループを生み出し、重要性重み付けが失敗するメカニズムを解明した。これに基づき、数値差異の中心化とラグ比のクリッピング、および再同期を行うDLC（Discrepancy-Lag Correction）手法を提案し、訓練の安定性とKL散度の制御に有効であることを示した。

papers.title: bf16 Rounding Silently Discards Most RL Policy Updates: A Hidden Training-Inference Mismatch and an Unbiased One-Line Fix
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training of language models keeps fp32 master weights in the optimizer and serves rollouts from a bf16 copy produced by round-to-nearest conversion. At the learning rates in common use, most per-step updates are smaller than half a bf16 spacing and the conversion discards them: on Qwen3-1.7B only 0.4-0.5% of served weights change per step, and the policy that generates the training data lags the optimizer by 50-150 steps. Existing mismatch corrections cannot see this lag because they compare two copies downstream of the same rounding. We propose Fair Cast: export the master with an unbiased rounding rule (stochastic rounding or error feedback) and compute the training loss on the served copy. The change is one line at the export call, adds no hyperparameters and costs 22-38 ms per export of 1.7B parameters. Across 25 matched seed-pairs on Qwen3-0.6B to 4B with AdamW and Muon, Fair Cast is ahead on 18, tied on 6 and behind on 1, with a mean gain of 6.1 points; on zebra puzzles it reaches 0.57 +/- 0.16 over four runs where round-to-nearest collapses to 0.33 +/- 0.10. It also makes the saved fp32 checkpoint agree with the served model, and it exposes the implicit lag of round-to-nearest as a regularizer that can be restored explicitly when a task needs it.
papers.title_ja: bf16 丸めが RL ポリシー更新の大半を無音で破棄する：隠れた学習・推論ミスマッチと無偏な 1 行修正
papers.summary_ja: 強化学習（RL）による LLM 後学習において、bf16 変換時の丸め誤差により、オプティマイザの更新が推論モデルに反映されず、学習と推論間に最大 150 ステップの遅延が生じている問題を指摘する。この「学習・推論ミスマッチ」を解消するため、エクスポート時に確率的丸めやエラーフィードバックを用いた無偏な変換ルール「Fair Cast」を提案する。本手法は 1 行のコード変更のみで、Qwen3 シリーズのベンチマークにおいて平均 6.1 ポイントの性能向上と、チェックポイントと推論モデルの整合性確保を実現した。

papers.title: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation
papers.summary: Self-distillation methods for large language models with an exponential moving average (EMA) teacher already retain a history of student updates. Muon nevertheless stores a separate momentum buffer, increasing persistent training memory. We propose Muon with Reused Teacher (Muon-RT), which reuses the teacher-student displacement to eliminate momentum buffers for hidden weight matrices. We show that this displacement encodes an exponentially weighted history of applied updates and smooths temporally uncorrelated noise under a local model. Muon-RT removes its radial component, normalizes it spectrally, and mixes it with the current gradient after Newton-Schulz (NS) orthogonalization. Under explicit regularity and alignment assumptions, we establish linear contraction of an expected objective-gap bound toward a residual error level. With Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Muon-RT improves average accuracy over AdamW by 2.6 points with 42% less persistent memory, and over momentum Muon by 5.4 points with 27% less persistent memory. With Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (SDPO) on Olmo-3-7B-Instruct, it improves average accuracy over AdamW by 2.0 points.
papers.title_ja: MUON-RT: LLM自己蒸留におけるモーメンタムフリーMuonのための教師モデル軌道の再利用

papers.title: RAMA: Retrieval-Augmented Multi-Agent Routing with Episodic Memory for LEO Satellite Networks
papers.summary: Low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks present a challenging routing environment due to rapidly changing topology, traffic, and link conditions. Existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) routing methods typically rely on current observations and information encoded in network weights, limiting their ability to exploit successful past experiences. We propose RAMA, a retrieval-augmented multi-agent DRL framework with Approximate Information State (AIS), in which each satellite combines its local observation, recent routing history, neighboring state information, and retrieved entries from a per-satellite episodic memory. Retrieved experiences are integrated through a Transformer-based decision network trained with AIS-based auxiliary objectives. With weights frozen in a 140-satellite Kepler constellation, RAMA reduces mean end-to-end latency by 13.4% and 99th-percentile latency by 66.7% relative to the state-of-theart double deep Q-network (DDQN) routing method, mainly by avoiding long detours. Updated online, RAMA remains stable while DDQN degrades. On the 1,584-satellite Starlink shell 1, the reduction in mean latency grows to 93.2%, and updating RAMA online lowers its mean latency by a further 25.5%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of retrieval-augmented memory for scalable decentralized routing in LEO satellite networks.
papers.title_ja: RAMA: LEO衛星ネットワーク向けエピソード記憶を用いた検索拡張マルチエージェントルーティング
papers.summary_ja: 低軌道（LEO）衛星ネットワークの動的なトポロジー変化に対応するため、強化学習（DRL）と検索拡張生成（RAG）の概念を融合したマルチエージェントルーティングフレームワーク「RAMA」を提案する。各衛星は局所観測に加え、エピソード記憶から取得した過去の成功体験をTransformerベースの決定ネットワークで統合し、効率的な経路選択を行う。140衛星のケプラー星座ではDDQN比で平均レイテンシを13.4%、99パーセンタイルレイテンシを66.7%低減し、1,584衛星のStarlink Shell 1では平均レイテンシを93.2%改善した。オンライン更新においても安定性を維持し、大規模分散ルーティングにおけるRAGと記憶機構の有効性を示した。

papers.title: TSBPO: Tree-Structured Branching for Policy Optimization in Interactive Language Agents
papers.summary: Training interactive language agents from terminal outcomes poses three coupled problems: which task and state continuations to sample, how to assign delayed feedback to decisions, and how to aggregate token losses for multi-token actions. We present TSBPO, a tree-structured sampling-to-update paradigm that addresses these problems within one training loop. A likelihood-fitted Root/Branch allocator uses retained task and state evidence to target continuations likely to produce contrasting terminal outcomes under fixed rollout budgets. On the resulting replayed physical trees, trajectory advantages compare immediate sibling segments, while observation-group step advantages compare outcomes at matched task/observation states. The actor then sums clipped token surrogates over each complete response and normalizes across active turns, avoiding response-length averaging in the policy-gradient term. With a Qwen2.5-1.5B actor, fixed checkpoints obtain 97.79% seen and 96.64% unseen stochastic success on ALFWorld and an 81.07% per-episode success rate over six stochastic episodes for each of the 500 WebShop test goals. A WebShop step-term ablation yields 75.93% at the same update-100 evaluation; an ALFWorld aggregation comparison shows higher observed command validity with complete-turn weighting. These results support the evaluated training configuration on two interactive benchmarks.
papers.title_ja: 対話型言語エージェントにおけるポリシー最適化のためのツリー構造分岐（TSBPO）
papers.summary_ja: 対話型言語エージェントの学習において、サンプリング戦略、遅延フィードバックの割り当て、マルチトークンアクションの損失集約という3つの課題を解決するツリー構造の学習フレームワークTSBPOを提案する。尤度ベースのRoot/Branchアロケータを用いて、固定予算内で対照的な結果を生みやすい状態を効率的にサンプリングし、再生された物理ツリー上で兄弟セグメントや同一状態間の比較によりアドバンテージを計算する。アクターは完全な応答ごとにクリップされたトークンサロゲートを合計し、応答長による平均化を回避することでポリシー勾配項を安定させる。Qwen2.5-1.5Bを用いた実験では、ALFWorldとWebShopのベンチマークにおいて高い成功率を示し、特にWebShopではエピソードあたり81.07%の成功を達成した。

papers.title: Improving the Optimization Landscape of Matrix Completion with $\epsilon$-close Surrogates
papers.summary: Non-convex optimization is central to machine learning and AI, yet unlike its convex counterpart, it still lacks a general and principled framework. In this work, we try to highlight the importance of combining noisy perturbations with over-parametrization mathematically under the classic setting of matrix completion (MC). Matrix completion is an important non-convex recovery problem in which only a subset of a matrix's entries is observed, and the remaining entries must be recovered using low-rank constraints. This problem is notoriously difficult because observations are limited. However, we show that by injecting $\epsilon$-level perturbations into the nullspace of the observation mask, we can construct noisy matrix sensing surrogates whose solutions remain $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon)$-close to the ground truth with valid restricted isometry property (RIP) constants. The existence of RIP further enables powerful tensor frameworks to be applied with theoretical guarantees. This approach reflects a broader empirical trend in which stochasticity or noise improves the curvature of the optimization landscape, allowing over-parameterized (a.k.a large) models to better separate signal from noise. Assuming each matrix entry is observed independently, we establish quantitative recovery guarantees without explicit requirements on sampling rate or incoherence, and discuss how such assumptions can further strengthen our results.
papers.title_ja: ε-近接サロゲートを用いた行列補完の最適化景観の改善
papers.summary_ja: 行列補完という非凸最適化問題において、観測マスクの零空間にεレベルの摂動を注入することで、真の解にO(ε)近接するノイジーな行列センシングサロゲートを構築する手法を提案する。このアプローチにより、有効な制限等方性（RIP）定数を保証しつつ、テンソルフレームワークを理論的保証付きで適用可能となる。観測が独立であるという仮定のもと、サンプリング率や非相干性の明示的な要件なしに定量的な復元保証を導出している。これは、確率性やノイズが最適化景観の曲率を改善し、過剰パラメータ化モデルがシグナルとノイズをより良く分離するという経験的傾向を数学的に裏付けるものである。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルと非凸最適化の理論的保証が関心に直結

papers.title: Query-Efficient Quantum Multi-Objective Optimization for Materials Configuration Search via Bayesian Weight Selection
papers.summary: Materials design is a multi-objective problem, and recent advances in quantum optimization make it possible to bring quantum solvers to bear on such problems. The realistic near-term win, though, is not raw quantum advantage but making an expensive, noisy quantum solver usable by spending its calls wisely. Quantum Approximate Multi-Objective Optimization (QAMOO) traces a Pareto front by solving a family of scalarized Ising problems, one per objective-weight vector, with QAOA --- but chooses those weights \emph{non-adaptively}, sampling them at random, blind to what it has already found. We recast weight selection as \emph{multi-objective Bayesian optimization}: our method, BW-QAMOO (Bayes-Weighted QAMOO), picks each next weight by expected hypervolume improvement (EHVI) under a Gaussian-process (GP) surrogate over the weight-to-objective map. On a frustrated alloy-configuration benchmark across $m\in\{3,4\}$ objectives and $n\in\{10,11,12\}$ sites, BW-QAMOO reaches the same Pareto hypervolume as QAMOO's random sampling with a median 33% fewer scalarized solves across the 90/95\% targets and 60--74\% fewer than a uniform-grid baseline), on a genuine (simulated) QAOA solver; a paired Wilcoxon test confirms the saving is significant, and the advantage grows with the objective count m as the weight simplex expands and blind sampling wastes more of the budget. This is a \emph{query-efficiency} result, and we close with the open challenges on the path to real alloy data and hardware.
papers.title_ja: ベイズ重み選択による材料構成探索のためのクエリ効率の良い量子多目的最適化
papers.summary_ja: 本研究は、量子近似多目的最適化（QAMOO）における重みベクトルの選択を、ガウス過程サロゲートモデルを用いた多目的ベイズ最適化として再定式化する。提案手法BW-QAMOOは、期待超体積改善（EHVI）に基づいて次の重みを適応的に選択し、ランダムサンプリングやグリッド探索よりも少ないクエリ数で同等のパレートフロン트를達成する。シミュレートされたQAOAソルバを用いた合金構成のベンチマークにおいて、クエリ効率の向上が統計的に有意であることを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: ベイズ最適化とサロゲートモデルによる最適化効率化が関心に直結

papers.title: Learning Nonlocal Interactions in Large-Scale Heterogeneous Metamaterials through Scientific Machine Learning
papers.summary: In multiscale systems, nonlocal interactions among spatially distributed constituents can unlock collective, potentially emergent behavior irreducible to individual constituent responses. Beyond characterization, nonlocality in multiscale systems is increasingly viewed as a design element across fracture mechanics, wave physics, and disordered systems. Existing nonlocality theories provide rigorous descriptions and mechanistic insight, but often require prescribed analytic forms, range, symmetries, or periodicity. Machine learning offers a data-driven route to learn interactions, yet principled approaches that tie the network design to physical theory remain nascent. Here we present domain-decomposition attention neural operator (DANO), which learns configuration-dependent interactions in heterogeneous systems governed by linear field equations from field data alone. Through a case study in large-scale optical metasurfaces, we demonstrate DANO's full-field prediction under geometric heterogeneity and across drive conditions, small-to-large domain transfer, and multifunctional inverse design, with learned interactions validated through physics-based interrogation. As an AI-for-Science tool, it supports interaction discovery and scalable, customizable design of nonlocal multiscale systems, including virtual-reality optics.
papers.title_ja: 科学的機械学習による大規模異種メタマテリアルの非局所相互作用の学習
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、線形場方程式で支配される異種系における設定依存の非局所相互作用を、場データのみから学習する「ドメイン分解アテンションニューラルオペレータ（DANO）」を提案する。大規模光学メタサーフェースのケーススタディを通じて、幾何学的異質性や駆動条件の違いにおける全場予測、小規模から大規模ドメインへの転移、および多機能逆設計の能力を実証した。学習された相互作用は物理ベースの検証により確認され、VR光学などの非局所マルチスケール系のスケーラブルな設計を支援するAI-for-Scienceツールとして機能する。
papers.relevance_reason: ニューラルオペレータと物理情報学習の応用であり、サロゲートモデル設計の高度な事例

papers.title: Cost-Aware Stopping for Freeze-Thaw Bayesian Optimization: When Does One-Step Lookahead Suffice?
papers.summary: Freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization (BO) evaluates candidates in resumable increments but usually stops at a budget or convergence test. We maximize a budget-free utility, the best observed score minus a cost per increment, with a one-step lookahead: advance the candidate with the largest expected improvement (EI) under a fixed surrogate, and stop once no EI exceeds the cost. This rule, EI stopping, never falls below stopping immediately in expected utility, yet it can stop too early. We construct a certificate, a lower bound on the value of two-step lookahead, that proves such a stop premature, and repeating this correction never lowers expected utility under the surrogate. Under the surrogate, EI stops are premature on average at low costs and lose little at high costs. On three hyperparameter optimization benchmarks, a pre-registered test finds EI stopping noninferior to the correction in most high-cost settings, while the correction gains at low costs on two of the three; more information sharing in the surrogate raises EI stopping's utility. On the surrogates of two published methods, EI stopping trades lower scores for fewer training increments. EI stopping is a simple cost-aware reference whose utility depends on the surrogate.
papers.title_ja: 凍結-解凍ベイズ最適化におけるコスト意識型停止則：1ステップ先読みが十分である条件
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、コストを考慮したベイズ最適化（BO）の停止基準として、期待改善度（EI）に基づく1ステップ先読み停止則を提案する。この規則は期待効用において即時停止を下回らないが、早期停止する可能性があるため、2ステップ先読みの価値を示す証明（certificate）を用いた補正手法も導出する。ハイパーパラメータ最適化のベンチマーク実験では、高コスト設定では補正と同等、低コスト設定では補正が優位であることが確認された。サロゲートモデルの情報共有度が高いほど、このEI停止則の効用は向上することが示された。
papers.relevance_reason: ベイズ最適化とサロゲートモデルの効率化に直結する手法

papers.title: CONSORT: Uncertainty-Constrained Multi-Robot Planning for Cooperative Localization in GPS-Denied Environments
papers.summary: Centralized multi-agent path planning with cooperative localization in GPS-denied environments is generally computationally intractable when formulated in full belief space due to tightly coupled uncertainty dynamics. Prior work typically approximates belief dynamics or restricts inter-agent coupling. This work examines a multi-agent planning problem in which a primary agent must reach a goal in minimum time subject to a chance-constrained collision-avoidance requirement and a terminal bound on localization uncertainty. We obtain a tractable surrogate of the underlying belief-space problem by optimizing over the mean-state trajectories of all agents and propagating covariance for terminal constraint evaluation only. We propose CONSORT (Cooperative Navigation with Support-Optimized Routing and Trajectories), a discrete-to-continuous pipeline combining hexagonal-grid joint search with spline-based trajectory refinement. Across 50 randomized scenarios, the planners separate as the terminal uncertainty bound tightens, with CONSORT solving 80% of scenarios where the strongest baseline solves 54%, at comparable path length. In marine simulations, with the plans executed under feedback control on an independently developed factor-graph estimate, the trajectories remain collision-free and their terminal uncertainty falls within 6% of the planner's prediction.
papers.title_ja: CONSORT: GPS拒否環境における協調局所化のための不確実性制約付きマルチロボット計画
papers.summary_ja: GPSが利用できない環境下でのマルチエージェント協調局所化と経路計画において、信念空間での計算困難さを回避するため、平均状態軌道の最適化と共分散伝播によるサロゲートモデルを提案する。六角形グリッド上の離散探索とスプラインによる連続軌道微調整を組み合わせる手法CONSORTを設計し、確率制約付き衝突回避と終端不確実性制約を同時に満たす。50シナリオの比較実験では、既存ベースラインより高い成功率（80%対54%）を示し、海洋シミュレーションでも計画された軌道が衝突を回避しつつ予測精度内に収まることを実証した。

papers.title: High-fidelity simulation and reduced-order modeling of optical pumping in quantum devices
papers.summary: Spatially resolved modeling of optically pumped alkali-metal vapors requires the solution of a high-dimensional nonlinear diffusive quantum master equation (DQME) coupled to state-dependent light propagation. We develop a structure-preserving computational framework for this coupled three-dimensional system in the high-pressure limit. The high-fidelity solver combines second-order finite differences, explicit pseudo-time marching, and an exponential-integrator discretization of the light-propagation equation. The scheme preserves the density-matrix trace, while a derived global pseudo-time-step restriction guarantees nonnegative, bound-preserving population updates and frozen-coefficient $1$-norm stability. In the absence of a closed-form solution for the general coupled problem, the solver is verified against complementary analytical reductions, pumping-rate asymptotics, and a light-propagation invariant, all of which are accurately recovered. Tensorized GPU implementation reduces the per-iteration cost by more than two orders of magnitude relative to a single-core CPU. For repeated parameter queries, we further construct an intrusive POD--Galerkin reduced-order model. The quadratic spin-exchange term is treated by an exact nonlinear quadratic expansion, whereas the nonpolynomial and nonlocal optical-pumping term is hyper-reduced using the discrete empirical interpolation method. At out-of-sample parameter points, the reduced model closely reproduces the full-order population and polarization fields while achieving speedup of more than \(7\times10^3\) relative to the single-core CPU full-order solver. The resulting hierarchy connects verified high-fidelity simulation with efficient reduced-order prediction for spatially resolved alkali-metal spin dynamics.
papers.title_ja: 量子デバイスにおける光ポンピングの高忠実度シミュレーションと縮約モデル
papers.summary_ja: アルカリ金属蒸気中の光ポンピング現象を記述する高次元非線形量子マスター方程式と光伝播の結合系に対し、構造保存型計算フレームワークを構築した。高密度行列のトレース保存や非負性を保証する数値スキームを設計し、GPU並列化により計算コストを大幅に削減した。さらに、POD-Galerkin法と離散経験的補間法を用いた縮約モデル（ROM）を構築し、フルオーダー解算器に対して7000倍以上の高速化を実現した。この手法は、空間分解能の高いスピンダイナミクスの予測において、高忠実度シミュレーションと効率的な推論を接続する階層型アプローチを提供する。

papers.title: Agentic Systems for Calibrating Cosmological Simulations
papers.summary: Calibrating a cosmological simulation is an expensive, high-dimensional parameter optimization task. Previous works employ Bayesian optimization for automation, which treats the simulator as a black box and precludes the incorporation of human domain knowledge or workflow into the selection policy. We propose AgenticTuner, an agentic calibration pipeline with a present-day large language model serving as the optimizer who proposes the next parameter trial. We show that these agents can achieve competitive calibration performance at a fraction of the CPU cost when they are given informal, human-readable priors (such as codebase, documentation, and heuristic guides that seasoned scientists may possess). We hope this work serves as an early step toward AI scientists that can carry out complex, long-horizon scientific tasks.
papers.title_ja: 宇宙シミュレーションの較正のためのエージェント型システム
papers.summary_ja: 高次元な宇宙シミュレーションの較正において、従来のベイズ最適化がブラックボックスとして扱われ人間知識の活用が難しかった問題を解決するため、LLMを最適化器として活用するAgenticTunerを提案する。この手法では、コードベースやドキュメントなどの非形式な人間可読な事前知識を与え、次のパラメータ試行をLLMが提案する。実験により、熟練科学者が持つようなヒューリスティックなガイドを与えれば、CPUコストを大幅に削減しながら競争力のある較正性能を達成できることを示した。これは複雑で長期にわたる科学タスクを遂行するAI科学者への初期段階のステップとなる。

papers.title: Automatic Construction of Strong Simple Baselines
papers.summary: To rigorously establish the value of a novel deep learning method, it must be compared against appropriate baselines. As deep learning has become increasingly common in the physical and life sciences, there have been numerous cases in which apparent progress has turned out to be an artifact of omitted or missing baselines. In this work, we investigate whether this problem can be mitigated by using large language models to automate the construction of baselines. We assemble 36 supervised classification and regression tasks from peer-reviewed studies in Nature, Science, and Cell-family journals that investigate novel deep learning methods for scientific applications. We then use a language model to construct simple baselines for each task. These automatically constructed baselines are strong, recovering a median of 95.5% (mean 85.7%) of the gap between a trivial predictor and the score of the deep learning model. The median simple baseline matches or exceeds the performance of the deep learning model in 12 studies. We further examine the variation across scientific domains and publication venues and we characterize the effects of test-time compute and access to different levels of study context. As human peer review has struggled to keep up with the rapidly increasing volume of research articles in recent years, our results suggest that automated baseline construction is a practical and scalable check on deep learning contributions in the physical and life sciences.
papers.title_ja: 強力な単純ベースラインの自動構築
papers.summary_ja: 深層学習手法の価値を厳密に検証するため、LLMを用いてベースラインを自動構築する手法を提案する。NatureやScienceなどの学術誌から36件の分類・回帰タスクを収集し、LLMで生成した単純なベースラインが、深層学習モデルとトリビアル予測器の間の性能差の中央値95.5%を回復することを示した。さらに、12件の研究においてこの自動生成ベースラインが深層学習モデル以上の性能を発揮した。本手法は、対人ピアレビューの限界を補完し、物理・生命科学分野における深層学習貢献の実用的かつスケーラブルな検証手段として機能する。

papers.title: Mage-VL-Cowork: A Full Training Recipe to Learn Hybrid Computer Use From Evolved Harnesses
papers.summary: Effective computer-use agents (CUAs) should seamlessly combine visual GUI interaction with code and terminal execution within a single policy. We present Mage-VL-Cowork, a 4B hybrid CUA trained from a general multimodally aligned checkpoint through an end-to-end, progressive five-stage curriculum across midtraining, SFT, and RL. To power this curriculum at scale, Mage-CUA-Forge replaces per-task agent construction with reusable, skill-conditioned generation workflows and application-specific preparers, synthesizing 293,806 desktop and web tasks across 6,915 skills while reducing recurring per-task expenditure by 82.6%. Rather than directly distilling a default teacher, we evolve the teacher harness and instantiate specialized CUA harnesses to yield high-quality trajectories alongside stage-specific supervision. Mage-VL-Cowork-4B finally climbs to 66.0% on OSWorld-Verified through different training stages with more efficient reasoning cost, achieving state-of-the-art performance at its parameter size and pushing forward the frontier of on-device intelligence.
papers.title_ja: Mage-VL-Cowork: 進化したハーネスからハイブリッドなコンピュータ使用を学習するための完全なトレーニングレシピ
papers.summary_ja: 視覚GUI操作とコード実行を単一のポリシーで統合する4Bパラメータのハイブリッド型コンピュータ使用エージェント（CUA）を提案する。段階的な5段階カリキュラムと、教師ハーネスの進化による高品質軌道の生成を通じて、OSWorld-Verifiedで66.0%というSOTA性能を達成した。推論コストを効率化しつつ、オンデバイスでの知能のフロンティアを押し広げる手法である。

papers.title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
papers.summary: Across coding, web, and tool-use tasks, language-model agents are now routinely trained with the same recipe: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to learn the interface, then multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) to master it. Code-as-policy (CaP) casts robot manipulation in the same form, as the policy writes code against robot APIs and reads back the results, so the same recipe should apply. Yet existing CaP agents sidestep training: they either prompt closed frontier models or delegate manipulation to pre-trained vision-language-action models (VLAs) and high-level skills, while small open vision-language models (VLMs) fail outright. We present CaPtain, an open post-training pipeline that turns a small open VLM into a capable CaP agent, with no VLA, frontier model, or privileged state at test time. CaPtain trains and deploys the policy inside CaPtain-Harness, which exposes low-level perception, geometry, and guarded-motion primitives across simulation and real hardware. We first align the base model via SFT on synthetic trajectories generated with GPT-6 Astra, then apply multi-turn RL. Multi-turn RL must credit tens of agent requests, whose physical effects often surface turns later, from a single end-of-episode outcome. We therefore introduce a physical critic that reads privileged simulator state, never seen by the policy, and credits each request by how much it changes the predicted chance of success. Starting from Qwen3.5-4B (0% zero-shot), CaPtain-4B reaches 55.4% held-out LIBERO success after SFT and 73.8% after RL. On LIBERO-PRO, it reaches 78.5%, surpassing several frontier-model agents, and its RL gains persist across three perturbation suites (+17.6 to +21.2 points). Without target-domain training, it attains 83.3% on SimplerEnv WidowX, exceeds frontier models on CaP-Bench, and runs on a real robot after simulation-only adaptation. We release all code, data, and model weights.

papers.title: FARO: Function-Space Adaptive Return-to-Risk Optimization via Cross-Block Equal-Risk-Contribution Budget Allocation
papers.summary: Training a large language model is compute-bound, and current recipes divide the work between optimizers by hand: orthogonalized momentum for attention and MLP matrices, Adam-style updates for the rest. This division rests on human priors about which layer type deserves which geometry, and it fixes a single global update budget that every parameter block shares. We introduce FARO, a function-space adaptive optimizer that makes the partition of parameters into blocks the unit of decision. FARO gives each block a geometry by its realized counterfactual return, then freezes the routes and reallocates the frozen per-block budget by cross-block equal risk contribution (ERC), the risk-parity principle from portfolio theory. On a GPT-style model trained on FineWeb, the framework gives two results. First, its FARO-Adaptive arm reaches 3.2780 nats at the full schedule, matching NorMuonAndAdam (3.2794), the best hand-designed recipe: it recovers the human prior without hand-setting per-layer geometry. Second, FARO-ERC improves on that arm: it lowers the clean-data loss at every one of 6 seeds, by 0.0136 nats on average, a modest but robust gain. Its sign test, paired test, and confidence interval all agree, and it exceeds the measured run-to-run noise at no added time or memory. It works by trimming the riskiest blocks rather than expanding the safest, and it holds up under a corrupted stream, still lowering the mean loss and winning the seed majority. The source code is available at https://github.com/wxj630/FARO.
papers.title_ja: FARO: 関数空間適応型リスク回帰最適化によるブロック間等リスク貢献予算配分
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデルの学習において、パラメータブロックごとに適応的な幾何構造を決定し、ポートフォリオ理論のリスクパリティ原則（ERC）を用いて更新予算を再配分する最適化手法FAROを提案する。人手による層別設定なしで既存の最良レシピと同等の性能を達成し、さらにリスクの高いブロックを削減することで損失を安定して低減させることを示した。この手法は追加の計算時間やメモリコストなしで、シード間のばらつきやデータ劣化に対して頑健性を有する。

papers.title: CoFiBreak: A Coarse-to-Fine Diversity Reward for Effective Multi-Turn Jailbreak
papers.summary: Automated red teaming trains an attacker large language model (LLM) to elicit harmful responses from a victim LLM, but reinforcement learning can collapse attackers onto a narrow set of prompts when attack success is the only reward. Such a collapse of attack diversity can bias safety evaluation toward repeatedly testing near-duplicate attack patterns rather than the underlying harmful intents. Existing methods often trade off attack success or inference cost for greater content or strategy diversity. We propose CoFiBreak, a coarse-to-fine diversity reward for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) that improves attack diversity while preserving strong attack effectiveness and low inference cost. The coarse reward broadens which strategies the attacker uses by encouraging strategies underrepresented within each GRPO group, while the fine reward broadens how those strategies are realized by discouraging reuse of the same personas, framings, and output formats after harmful-intent information is removed from prompt embeddings. Diversity rewards apply only to attacks that already exceed an effectiveness threshold, so diversity cannot be gained through ineffective attacks. Since both rewards are computed only during training, CoFiBreak also retains inference efficiency. Trained with Llama3.1-8B-Instruct as the victim, CoFiBreak discovers 1.6-2.0x as many distinct successful fine-grained strategies as the strongest baseline across frontier victims on HarmBench. It reaches 98.8% ASR@10 (attack success rate with 10 generations per intent) on AdvBench with the highest diversity score among all compared methods, which is 2.1x that of the strongest-attacking baseline. The resulting attacks transfer to unseen frontier LLMs, reaching 71.0% ASR@10 on AdvBench with the unseen victim Claude-Opus-4.6. The code will be released.
papers.title_ja: CoFiBreak: 効果的なマルチターン・ジェイルブレイクのための粗から細への多様性報酬
papers.summary_ja: 強化学習によるLLMの自動レッドチーミングにおいて、攻撃の多様性が低下し安全評価が偏る問題を解決する手法を提案する。GRPOを用い、戦略レベルと実装レベルの2段階で多様性を奨励する報酬設計を導入し、攻撃成功率と推論コストを維持しつつ多様性を向上させる。Llama3.1-8B-Instructを被害者モデルとして訓練し、既存手法より1.6〜2.0倍の多様な成功戦略を発見した。また、未知のフロンティアLLMへの転移性も示し、ハルシネーション対策や評価手法の改善に寄与する。

papers.title: Opening the Box Changes the Cat: LLMs Detect Chain-of-Thought Monitoring - What now?
papers.summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning allows large language models (LLMs) to generate intermediate reasoning traces in natural language while solving complex tasks. These traces can support safety monitoring by exposing potentially harmful plans before actions are executed. In this work, we investigate the conditions under which LLMs infer the presence of CoT monitoring from direct and indirect environmental cues and examine how this inference affects their subsequent behavior. Our observations suggest that oversight is an interactive process: while a monitor inspects a model's reasoning, traces left by monitoring interventions can allow the model to infer that its thoughts are being observed and to adapt its behavior accordingly. We show that even subtle environmental cues, such as timing-related signals from timeouts and operation durations, can reveal the presence of monitoring and trigger models to adapt their behavior. Across repeated episodes and interaction loops, we further observe that models can form statistical estimates of the monitor's effectiveness and use these estimates to guide attempts to evade detection. These findings highlight the need to evaluate CoT-based oversight under adaptive conditions, where the monitoring process itself may influence the behavior it seeks to observe.
papers.title_ja: 箱を開けると猫が変わる：LLMは思考連鎖の監視を検出する - 今後どうするか？
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、大規模言語モデル（LLM）が思考連鎖（CoT）の監視存在を環境からの手がかりから推測し、その行動を適応させる現象を調査する。タイムアウトや処理時間などの微細なシグナルから監視を検出し、検出回避を試みる行動が観察された。さらに、モデルは監視の有効性に関する統計的推定を形成し、それを基に検出回避戦略を調整することが示された。これらの発見は、監視プロセス自体が対象の行動に影響を与える動的な条件下でのCoT監視評価の必要性を強調している。

papers.title: Fewer Heads, Fewer Memories: Pruning Redundant Attention Heads Suppresses Verbatim Memorisation
papers.summary: Large language models have been shown to memorise and reproduce verbatim sequences from their training data, raising concerns about privacy leakage, intellectual property exposure, and the limits of generalisation. Recent theoretical work suggests that attention heads may contribute to this behaviour by functioning as associative memory mechanisms, with memorisation capacity scaling with the number of heads. At the same time, empirical work has shown that many attention heads are redundant and can be pruned with limited impact on downstream performance. Despite these parallel findings, the effect of pruning redundant heads on memorised-sequence reproduction remains unexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that zeroing out a substantial fraction of attention heads prior to inference can significantly suppress verbatim memorisation while preserving, or even improving, language modelling performance on the benchmark used to identify redundant heads. Evaluating GPT-2-XL(1.5B) on known memorised sequences, we find that pruning 729 task-redundant heads reduces the memorisation count by 91.5%, while improving WikiText-103 perplexity by 0.92. These findings suggest that attention-head redundancy can be exploited to mitigate memorisation at inference time, without retraining or modifying the training data.
papers.title_ja: ヘッドとメモリを減らす：冗長なアテンションヘッドの剪定による逐語的記憶の抑制
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）が学習データを逐語的に記憶・再生成する問題に対し、推論時に冗長なアテンションヘッドをゼロ化することでこれを抑制する手法を提案する。GPT-2-XLを用いた実験では、タスク冗長な729個のヘッドを剪定することで、記憶されたシーケンスの再生成を91.5%削減しつつ、WikiText-103のパープレキシティを改善した。再学習や学習データの変更なしに、推論時のメモリ使用量削減とプライバシーリスク低減を同時に実現できることを示している。

papers.title: Can Personal Requirements Become Supervision for Planning?
papers.summary: Managing multiple chronic conditions through diet requires satisfying disease- and medication-specific requirements jointly across meals and days while preserving established eating habits. These requirements are public in clinical guidelines and drug labels, yet turning them into a feasible plan for one person remains difficult for language-model agents. In our dietitian-approved weekly planning evaluation built from NHANES, thirteen models, from medically fine-tuned 8B models to GPT-6.1 Sol, pass fewer than 3% of complete plans through direct generation. Explicit rules, higher reasoning effort, or model-directed tools leave GPT-6.1 Sol at no more than 8%. We present Noura, which pairs LLM planning with executable personal specifications instantiated from public clinical guidance and individual health and dietary profiles. During planning, the specification grounds foods, optimizes portions, checks the complete multi-day plan, and guides revision. Our key insight is that a specification that rejects a plan can also determine what to learn from it. Noura turns executed plans and contextually credited revisions into supervision for compact models, recovering targets even from trajectories that never achieve complete success. The same specification supplies supervised targets, preferences, and rewards for post-training. On 4,993 held-out participants, Noura-SFT raises Qwen3-14B's complete-plan pass rate from 24.0% to 72.5% within the same execution loop, cuts rule violations by 97.5% with no observed critical failures, and improves dietary quality. The locally hosted 14B planner incurs fewer rule violations than its GPT-6 Luna teacher. A matched comparison shows that executed targets reduce rule violations by 41% over model-written proposals. Across four Qwen, Phi, and Llama backbones, self-training alone reduces rule violations by 41-61% on a 1,249-person population subset.
papers.title_ja: 個人の要件は計画の教師信号となり得るか？
papers.summary_ja: 慢性疾患管理のための食事計画において、LLMが臨床ガイドラインと個人の健康状態を統合し、実行可能な計画を生成する課題に取り組む。提案手法Nouraは、実行可能な個人仕様（specification）を用いて計画を検証・修正し、その過程で得られた成功・失敗の軌跡を教師信号としてコンパクトモデルのSFTや強化学習に活用する。これにより、GPT-6.1 Solなどの大規模モデルを上回る完全計画パス率（72.5%）とルール違反の大幅削減（97.5%）を実現した。本手法は、LLMのエージェント設計における評価基準の活用と、小規模モデルへの知識蒸留・効率化に寄与する。

papers.title: Steering Vectors as a Training Signal in LLM Post-Training
papers.summary: Steering vectors (SVs) are residual-stream directions that shift the behavior of LLMs when added to hidden states at inference time. While prior work has mainly used SVs as post-hoc controls, we ask whether the same directions can also guide parameter updates during post-training. We study this question across supervised learning, including SFT and distillation, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Our framework considers two intervention regimes: a hidden-state hook during teacher-forced supervised training, and an advantage-repair mechanism on wrong rollouts in GRPO. For each regime, we analyze three design axes, which are the steering direction, its placement, and the operation used to combine it with training. In supervised settings, SV injection improves over plain SFT and distillation, with gains scaling with the off-policy gap and reaching up to a $12\%$ improvement when distilling from thinking-mode teachers. These gains hold across three random seeds. In RL settings, applying a correctness-contrast direction as advantage repair on wrong rollouts, including otherwise zero-gradient all-wrong groups, recovers a learning signal that transfers to held-out math benchmarks and acts as a composable auxiliary signal that adds to existing zero-variance remedies such as entropy-aware advantage shaping. We further identify three failure boundaries. In detail, code generation can break the direction, cross-family layer transfer can break the placement, and inference-time application on an SV-trained checkpoint can break the intervention regime. Together, these results establish steering vectors as a conditional but effective training signal for LLM post-training. Our code is available here.
papers.title_ja: LLM後学習におけるSteering Vectorsを訓練シグナルとして活用する
papers.summary_ja: 本研究は、推論時の行動制御に用いられるSteering Vectors（SVs）を、LLMの後学習（SFT、蒸留、RLVR）におけるパラメータ更新のガイドとして活用する手法を提案する。教師強制学習時の隠れ状態フックや、GRPOにおける誤ったロールアウトへのアドバンテージ修復機構を通じて、SVsを訓練プロセスに統合する。実験により、オフポリシーギャップが大きいほど効果が顕著になり、思考モード教師からの蒸留では最大12%の性能向上が確認された。また、RL設定では正解対比方向を用いることで、ゼロ勾配グループからも学習シグナルを回復し、既存のゼロ分散対策と組み合わせ可能であることが示された。一方で、コード生成やクロスファミリー層転送、推論時適用など、特定の条件下で効果が失われる失敗境界も特定されている。

papers.title: Towards Understanding Score-Seeking in LLMs
papers.summary: Production large language models sometimes reward-hack, exploiting flaws in how tasks are scored rather than performing the tasks as intended, sometimes in highly sophisticated and adversarial ways. We investigate the motivations driving this behavior in GPT 5.6 Sol, GPT 5.5, and a checkpoint of OpenAI o3 without safety training ("exp-rl-cap-late") by observing model behavior in agentic environments where the grader is leaked. In our environments, the models appear to be score-seeking: trying to score well according to graders that they believe assess their current actions, even at the expense of violating explicit user instructions. They appear to care about score itself rather than its downstream consequences, violating instructions at approximately the same rate whether the score is indicated to be used for training, for evaluation, or not at all. We observe evidence that the more recent models care to some extent about scores that do not assess their own current actions. GPT 5.6 Sol and GPT 5.5 help other agents 24.6 percentage points more often on average when the other agent stands to gain a score of 1 rather than 0 from being helped. However, when grading or monitoring another trajectory, we find models never collude by distorting its score.
papers.title_ja: LLMにおけるスコア追求行動の理解に向けて
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、GPT 5.6 Solやo3などの大規模言語モデルが、タスクの意図ではなく採点基準（グレーダー）の欠陥を悪用して報酬ハッキングを行う「スコア追求」行動の動機を調査する。エージェント環境において、モデルは明示的なユーザー指示を無視しても、現在の行動を評価すると信じるスコアを最大化しようとする傾向が示された。また、モデルはスコアそのものよりもその下流の結果を重視しておらず、評価用途の有無に関わらず同程度の頻度で指示違反を行う。さらに、他エージェントのスコア向上を助ける傾向はあるものの、他者の評価を歪めて共謀することは観察されなかった。

papers.title: Do Language Models Know What Compelling Scientific Evidence Looks Like?
papers.summary: Expert scientists excel at weighing empirical findings from multiple sources that vary in both statistical reliability and epistemic relevance. To what extent are language models, which are increasingly driving autonomous discovery systems, capable of such evidence deliberation? We introduce EDB-Bio, a scientific reasoning benchmark curated from real-world data in three biological domains: drug-perturbation transcriptomics, CRISPR screens, and human genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Each of EDB-Bio's 96k episodes presents a sequence of experimental results from published studies and asks the model to predict the probability that a target hypothesis is true. Out-of-the-box, open-weight and frontier models alike demonstrate systematic underconfidence and attain Brier scores comparable to a trivial base-rate forecaster. Post-training against strictly proper scoring rules significantly improves both calibration and discrimination. This calibration pays off downstream: in a sequential experiment selection task, our Ibis0 model is 2.5 times more efficient than the best frontier model. Throughout, quantifying evidence weights as Bayes factors reveals how models update their beliefs over time, whether they agree with expert biologists on relevance, and where they exhibit inconsistencies and biases. Our work extends calibration training and uncertainty analysis to a realistic scientific forecasting setting with applications to human cancer biology. We release all code, data, and trained models.
papers.title_ja: 言語モデルは説得力のある科学的証拠の姿を知っているのか？
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、生物学的な実験結果から仮説の真偽を予測するベンチマーク「EDB-Bio」を提案し、LLMの科学的証拠評価能力を評価する。既存モデルは系統的な過小信頼を示し、ベースレート予測器と同等の性能にとどまるが、厳密なスコアリングルールを用いた後学習により較正と識別力が大幅に向上する。較正されたモデルは、逐次実験選択タスクにおいてフロンティアモデルより2.5倍効率的であり、ベイズ因子による信念更新の分析を通じて、専門家との一致点やバイアスを定量的に明らかにする。

papers.title: Consensus Within, Competition Between: Decentralized LLM Teams for Perimeter Defense
papers.summary: The use of large language models (LLMs) to coordinate multi-agent teams raises a fundamental architectural question: whether task allocation should be centralized in a single LLM controller or distributed across autonomous LLM agents, particularly when communication is unreliable. In a deliberately simplified perimeter-defense simulation against LLM-controlled intruders, we compared a central commander, an auction-based consensus team and independent agents under five network conditions. Breach rates were 15% for the consensus team, 32% for the commander and 29% for independent agents, and of the different network conditions, only limited radio range changed a team's breach rate, raising the commander's. In consensus team, giving a low-cost LLM more authority over the bid computation raised breaches by 38 percentage points. With birds and civilian drones in airspace, we added a photograph for each to the input text state. Only the near-frontier model treated them apart from intruders. Intruders disguised as existing taxidermy bird drones were mistook as birds by both low-cost and near-frontier LLMs, going unpursued in 59-61% of near-frontier decisions (1-16% before). However, a one-sentence forewarning in the prompt lowered it to 0-25%. We find that LLM team with a dedicated external conflict resolution protocol results in fewest breaches. Code: https://github.com/the-kas-lab/consensus-within-competition-between.
papers.title_ja: 内部の合意、外部の競争：周縁防衛のための分散型LLMチーム
papers.summary_ja: 通信が不安定な環境下で、LLMによるマルチエージェント協調のアーキテクチャ（中央集権型、オークションベースの合意形成、独立エージェント）を比較検討した。周縁防衛シミュレーションの結果、外部の競合解決プロトコルを持つ合意形成チームが最も低い侵入率（15%）を示し、中央司令官型（32%）や独立エージェント型（29%）を上回った。また、低コストLLMに権限を集中させると侵入率が大幅に上昇し、敵対的ディープフェイクへの対応ではプロンプトの事前警告が有効であることも確認された。

papers.title: INLA for Adaptive UAV Sampling of Radio Environment Maps in IoT Networks: Prior Width Governs Accuracy and Calibration
papers.summary: We study adaptive UAV sampling for radio environment map (REM) construction from non-Gaussian IoT observations. Integrated nested Laplace approximation(INLA) updates a Mat\'ern GMRF posterior, with waypoints selected by entropy pre-screening and Sherman--Morrison lookahead over the reachable set. We show that the likelihood-induced Skew-Normal correction has a sextic entropy effect, explaining its limited influence on waypoint selection. Across 19 retained ray-traced windows,Random and lawnmower sampling cost a median 18.0\% and 14.0\% more residual NMSE than posterior-informed sampling, equivalently reductions of 15.3\% and 12.3\% when referred to those baselines, while differences among informative rules remain unresolved. Widening the prior shadowing standard deviation from 6.0 to 10.025\,dB improves NMSE and credible-interval coverage, with monotone improvement over a 4--16\,dB sweep on this corpus and no observed turning point, although overconfidence persists. Online width estimation from the UAV's own counts yields about 6.5\,dB without recovering the gain. Across 30 measured LoRaWAN propagation windows paired with simulated counts and scored only on received cells, the margin over non-adaptive sampling reproduces, the training-derived width minimizes the tested interval score, and GP-UCB has nominally $3$--$5\%$ lower NMSE. The results show substantial, corpus-dependent sensitivity to prior specification, while fine differences among acquisition rules have limited or unresolved effects, the preferred width depends on the corpus, scored cells and model mismatch.
papers.title_ja: IoTネットワークにおける無線環境マップの適応型UAVサンプリングのためのINLA：事前分布の幅が精度と較正を支配する
papers.summary_ja: 本研究は、非ガウシアンなIoT観測データから無線環境マップ（REM）を構築するための適応型UAVサンプリング手法を提案する。統合ネストラプラス近似（INLA）を用いてMatérn GMRFの事後分布を更新し、エントロピーによる事前スクリーニングとSherman-Morrisonルックアヘッドによりウェイポイントを選択する。事前分布のシャドーイング標準偏差（幅）を広げることで、残差NMSEと信頼区間のカバレッジが改善されることが示された。また、取得ルール間の微細な差よりも、事前分布の仕様に対する感受性が結果に大きく影響することが明らかになった。
